title: A thousand merits, but no character
odia:
ଥିଲେ ଥାଉ ପଛେ ଗୁଣ ହଜାର
ଚରିତ୍ର ନଥିଲେ ସବୁ ଅସାର
literal_meaning: Even if there are a thousand merits, without character they are all worthless.
meaning_odia: ହଜାର ଗୁଣ ଥାଇ ମଧ୍ୟ ଚରିତ୍ର ନଥିଲେ ସେସବୁ ଅସାର—ଏହା ଏହି ବଚନର ଜୋରଦାର ମତ। ଆମ ବ୍ୟାଖ୍ୟାରେ, ଦକ୍ଷତା କିମ୍ବା ପ୍ରତିଭାକୁ ପ୍ରଶଂସା କଲାବେଳେ ସତତା ଓ ଆଚରଣକୁ ଅବହେଳା ନକରିବାର ତାଗିଦ ଏଥିରେ ଅଛି। ହଜାର ଓ ସବୁ ଅସାର କଥା ଦୁଇଟି ଏହି ତାଗିଦକୁ ତୀବ୍ର କରୁଛି।
explanation: The saying makes a forceful moral claim: however many merits someone has, character is what gives them value. We read its emphasis as a reminder to consider integrity alongside skill or talent. “A thousand” and “all worthless” belong to the verse’s absolute rhetoric, rather than a measured assessment of a person’s whole worth.
usage_example: Original imagined example: A committee admires someone’s ability but also has to consider evidence of dishonesty. A member recalls this saying to insist that ability alone should not settle the decision.
cultural_context: The contrast sets a large number of merits against one missing quality. The rhyme ହଜାର / ଅସାର turns that moral ranking into a short, memorable judgment.

english_summary: The saying ranks character above an abundance of other merits.
